messages:
Rafael Mendes: seeing a bunch of noisy pages from the guardrails pilot alerts over the last ~24h. Mostly `EvalRunnerLatencyHigh` + `GatingTimeoutRateHigh` firing when traffic is low. Can we tune before we add more pilot tenants?

Sean Gallagher: yep, got woken up twice :/ which alerts specifically? links?

Rafael Mendes: Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/opt-guardrails/optimize-guardrails-gating (pilot folder)
Panels that correlate w pages:
- Panel “Eval runner job latency (p50/p95)”
- Panel “Queue depth (jobs)”
- Panel “Gating outcome rates (pass/fail/timeout)”

Miles Thornton: I pulled alert history. It’s basically p95 latency > 30s for 10m. But during pilot we sometimes have like 8-12 jobs in a 10m window, so one slow suite blows it up.

Allison Grant: +1. current rules don’t have a min sample size guard. for pilot we should require `jobs_completed >= N` before evaluating ratio/quantile.

Logan Wright: data point: some of the “timeouts” are actually client-side deadline exceeded from console polling (60s) while the job completes at ~75-90s. so it’s not a runner outage, it’s mismatch between UI expectation and runner budget.

Nadia Rahman: do we know if these timeouts correlate with the heavy suites? quantization suite is the worst offender.

Rafael Mendes: yep. spikes line up with `quant_guardrails_v2` suite runs. panel “Latency by suite” shows p95 ~92s at the top of the hour.

Sean Gallagher: ok, so two things:
1) tune alerts to be less twitchy / only page on real outage
2) follow up w product/console to align timeouts (but that’s not this thread)

Miles Thornton: proposal for alert tuning (pilot stage):
- `EvalRunnerLatencyHigh` -> page if p95 > 120s for 20m AND `jobs_completed >= 50` in window
- add warning (no page) if p95 > 90s for 20m AND `jobs_completed >= 20`
- `GatingTimeoutRateHigh` -> only evaluate when `gating_decisions >= 30` in 30m; page if timeout_rate > 10% AND error_reason=runner_timeout (exclude `client_deadline`)

Allison Grant: +1 on excluding `client_deadline`. That’s a UX/timeout config issue, not infra.

Rafael Mendes: can we also change the queue depth page? it fired when backlog hit 140 for ~5 mins then recovered.

Sean Gallagher: what’s the current threshold?

Rafael Mendes: backlog > 100 for 5m (page). which seems too low for the worker autoscale behavior.

Miles Thornton: yeah we scale workers every 2 mins; backlog can transiently spike. maybe page on backlog > 500 for 15m + no drain.

Logan Wright: also note: queue depth cardinality is per region. the alert is aggregating all regions, which is fine for overall health but it’s amplifying noise when one region is doing eval backfills.

Allison Grant: can we make the page condition be “backlog increasing over 10m” vs absolute threshold? (slope)

Sean Gallagher: slope is nicer but harder to reason about when oncall. I’m ok w absolute + longer window.

Hannah Rivera: from rollout/rollback perspective, paging on small transient backlog isn’t useful. if runner is truly down we’ll see sustained backlog + rising timeouts + policy engine safe-degrade kicking in.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. another panel that seems more indicative is “Runner error rate (5xx)” + “Worker heartbeats”. those stayed clean during the pages.

Miles Thornton: ok concrete edits:
- `EvalRunnerQueueDepthHigh` page if `queue_depth > 750` for 20m OR `queue_depth > 400` for 30m (pilot)
- add non-paging alert for `queue_depth > 250` for 15m (so we notice)

Allison Grant: and add annotation in the dashboard for the pilot: “low-N makes quantiles noisy; alerts use min_jobs guardrails”.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. let’s also update runbook link in the alert to point to the right section (it currently points to generic eval-harness runbook).

Rafael Mendes: I can patch the alert rules in observability-pack today. will open PR and tag @Allison Grant for review.

Logan Wright: pls also update the dashboard panel for “timeouts” to split by `timeout_source` (runner vs client). I can do the metric label change on telemetry side but for now we can use existing `reason` field.

Nadia Rahman: do we want an alert for “hard-block rate increases” during pilot? feels like a product KPI, but it’s currently paging too.

Sean Gallagher: we should not page on hard-block rate in pilot. make it a dashboard-only KPI + maybe a daily digest. page only for system health (runner/policy engine).

Miles Thornton: +1. hard-blocking can be legit (quality regression) and should go to the owning team, not wake SRE.

Rafael Mendes: cool. action items:
- Rafael: PR to tune alerts (latency/backlog/timeout) + remove paging from hard-block KPI
- Allison: review rule changes + update dashboard annotations
- Logan: propose split of timeout reasons in metrics + follow-up ticket

Sean Gallagher: ship it. once merged, let’s monitor for 48h and see if pages stop while still catching real runner issues.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: will post PR link here when up
